items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I never was around Fats too much. We played a theatre opposite him, the Howard Theatre in Washington

ctx.x: Tell me about Fats Waller's band.

Well, he carried a big band, and he played all of the big theatres at this time, you know. And this was during the thirties, you know, and why I mentioned it is because normally, you know, one guy will come in to jam, you know, or maybe two, but Fats brought his whole 16 piece band in to jam. They took up the table space there was so many of them. This was -- the Three Deuces was really a small club. And they were appearing at the theatre right around on Randolph, I forget. But they came by and I remember the…

I never was around Fats too much. We played a theatre opposite him, the Howard Theatre in Washington, and after that and the one thing that impressed me then was they had to lead him on, he was so juiced, they would lead him on stage during the black out and sit him down and then the lights would come on with him sitting at the piano.
